name: Pathfinder 3 (servo/pathfinder)
baseline: unnamed 'best CPU rasterizers' and 'typical software renderers that use the painter's algorithm' (README names no product; Skia and Cairo are the implied software incumbents)
workload: GPU tile-based rasterization of fonts and vector paths (OpenGL 3.0+, GLES 3.0+, Metal), including many-overlapping-path SVG and PDF content, versus CPU rasterizers.
claimed_speedup: Directional only, no numbers: 'Even on lower-end GPUs, Pathfinder often matches or exceeds the performance of the best CPU rasterizers. The difference is particularly pronounced at large sizes, where Pathfinder regularly achieves multi-factor speedups.' Occlusion culling 'often results in dramatic performance wins over typical software renderers that use the painter's algorithm.'
tradeoffs: Needs a GPU with OpenGL 3.0+/GLES 3.0+ or Metal; it is a GPU rasterizer, not a CPU library. Subset canvas API and a simple resvg-based SVG loader, not a full Skia or Cairo replacement. Rust crates, so use from C++ needs FFI (C API not verified this session).
caveats: No numeric benchmark and no named baseline anywhere on the repo page, so this is tier D (notable project, widely referenced on HN). The latest commit on the commits page is a dependency bump (pathfinder_simd 0.5.5 to 0.5.6, #587), so activity is maintenance, not feature work. The same repo is already recorded under the font category (w10-font-papers, 'Pathfinder 3', tier D); this entry is the rasterizers-2d view of the same project. HN threads seen only as titles and snippets, not opened.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch (news.ycombinator.com) 'Show HN fast 2D vector graphics renderer' and 'Show HN 2D vector graphics library Zig OR Rust OR Go anti-aliased rasterizer faster than Cairo' surfaced the thread 'Pathfinder, a fast GPU-based font rasterizer in Rust' and several comments naming Pathfinder as the best free-software GPU path renderer; repo README opened on github.com (also via raw.githubusercontent.com).

name: Rasterizer (mindbrix)
baseline: unnamed CPU path rasterization ('the CPU'); README does not name the CPU renderer. HN discussion compared it against CoreGraphics (reference quality) and Vello (GPU compute)
workload: Metal GPU rendering of anti-aliased vector paths (SVG and PDF scenes, vector animated UI; HN thread snippet mentions text at 50,000 glyphs at 60fps) versus CPU rendering.
claimed_speedup: 'It is up to 60x faster than the CPU, making it ideal for vector animated UI' (README opening paragraph, no workload, hardware or baseline stated).
tradeoffs: Targets macOS with C++11 and Metal only (iOS port in progress; README says it would work on any GPU with instancing and float render targets). Single font in the demo app. Custom 'personal use zlib license': personal use only, commercial use needs a licence from the author. Uses novel windowed-inverse-lerp area coverage and GPU quadratic Bezier solving.
caveats: Only number is the unqualified 'up to 60x faster than the CPU' with no baseline library, scene, hardware or flags; no benchmark code in the repo. License (LICENSE.txt: zlib terms plus 'for personal use (for a commercial licence please contact the author)') is not OSI-approved, hence reference, not copyable. HN thread 'Rasterizer: A GPU-accelerated 2D vector graphics engine in ~4k LOC' was seen only as a title and comment snippets (author compares against Vello and CoreGraphics MSAA), not opened. The ~4k LOC figure comes from the HN title and was not verified in the repo.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch (news.ycombinator.com) 'Show HN Rasterizer GPU-accelerated 2D vector graphics engine 4k LOC' surfaced the thread 'Rasterizer: A GPU-accelerated 2D vector graphics engine in ~4k LOC' (item 45090553); README, LICENSE.txt and commits page opened on github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com.
